t: The plant body of bryophytes is thallus-like, prostrate or erect and attached to substratum with the help of
s: Bryophytes lack true roots, stems and leaves. Their thallus-like, prostrate or erect plant body is attached to the substratum by rhizoids. In liverworts these are unicellular, while in mosses they are multicellular and branched. Roots, whether unicellular or multicellular, are absent in bryophytes.

t: In moss, the sporophyte is differentiated into
s: The moss sporophyte is differentiated into foot, seta and capsule. The foot is embedded in the gametophyte to absorb nutrients, the seta is a stalk, and the capsule produces spores by meiosis. Protonema is the juvenile gametophytic stage that develops from a spore, not part of the sporophyte.

t: In gymnosperms, the leaves are well-adapted to withstand extremes of temperature, humidity and wind. Which is/are the xeric character(s) of conifers?
s: Conifer leaves show xeric adaptations that reduce water loss: needle-like leaves give a small surface area, a thick cuticle reduces transpiration and the stomata are sunken in pits. All of these help them withstand extremes of temperature, humidity and wind, so all the given characters apply.

t: The dominant phase is the diploid sporophyte in which of the following groups
s: In pteridophytes, gymnosperms and angiosperms the main plant body is the diploid sporophyte, so it is the dominant phase. In bryophytes the haploid gametophyte is dominant and the sporophyte is dependent on it, while most algae have a dominant haploid gametophyte. Hence only option A lists groups that all have a dominant sporophyte.

t: Heterospory is found in some members of ____ and all members of ____.
s: Heterospory, the production of two kinds of spores (microspores and megaspores), occurs in only a few pteridophytes such as Selaginella and Salvinia, but in all gymnosperms (and angiosperms). Bryophytes are homosporous. So the blanks are filled by pteridophytes and gymnosperms.

t: Protonema stage represents the
s: In mosses the haploid spore germinates to form the protonema, a creeping, green, branched, often filamentous structure. It is the first or juvenile stage of the gametophyte, from which the leafy gametophyte develops as lateral buds. It is not sporophytic, and the gametophyte of ferns is the prothallus.
o: First stage of gametophyte in Mosses

t: Which one of the following statement concerning the algae is incorrect?
s: Algae are not all filamentous; they range from unicellular (Chlamydomonas) and colonial (Volvox) forms to filamentous (Ulothrix, Spirogyra) and massive forms like kelps. Most algae are photosynthetic, they are classified into classes on the basis of pigments, and red algae have no motile stages, so they do not produce zoospores.
o: Algae can be classified according to their pigments
Red algae does not produce zoospores

t:
Read the following statements and select the correct option :
Statement I : In Gymnosperms, the male and female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence.
Statement II : Pollination in Gymnosperms is by the agency of wind.
s: Both statements are true. In gymnosperms the male and female gametophytes have no independent free-living existence; they remain within the sporangia on the sporophyte. Pollen grains are released from microsporangia and carried by wind to the ovules, so gymnosperms are wind-pollinated.

t: Select a haploid structure in bryophyte:
s: The protonema develops directly from a haploid spore by mitosis, so it is part of the haploid gametophyte of mosses. Foot, seta and capsule together form the sporophyte, which develops from the diploid zygote and is diploid. Therefore protonema is the only haploid structure in the list.

t: Motile structures are not formed during any stage in the life cycle of
s: Red algae (Rhodophyceae) have no flagellated stages at all; their gametes and spores are non-motile, and the male gametes are carried passively by water currents. Green and brown algae form flagellated zoospores and gametes. Blue-green algae also lack flagella, but in the standard algal classification red algae are noted for having no motile stages.

t: Gymnosperms include
s: Gymnosperms include medium-sized trees, tall trees and shrubs; for example, Sequoia is one of the tallest trees. Herbaceous gymnosperms are not found, so herbs are excluded. Therefore gymnosperms include shrubs and medium-sized trees, i.e. all except option 1.

t: A type of classification which is based mainly on vegetative characters and based on a few characteristics:-
s: Artificial systems of classification, such as that of Linnaeus, were based on a few characteristics, mainly vegetative characters or the androecium structure. Natural systems use many characters including anatomy and chemistry, and phylogenetic systems are based on evolutionary relationships. Hence the description fits the artificial system.

t: Find out the mismatch
s: Pteridophytes are classified into Psilopsida (Psilotum), Lycopsida (Selaginella, Lycopodium), Sphenopsida (Equisetum) and Pteropsida (Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum). Selaginella belongs to Lycopsida, not Sphenopsida, so option D is the mismatch.

t:
Identify the Pteridophyte given in the following figure and select the statement which is false about it :
[[img:01da0dbb7cb6]]
s: The figure is Salvinia, an aquatic water fern. It is heterosporous and heterophyllous, bearing floating leaves and submerged dissected leaves that look like roots. True roots are absent in Salvinia, so the statement that it has true root, stem and leaves is false, while the other statements are true.
o: It possess two types of leaves
It possess true root, stem and leaves
They are aquatic fern which show heterospory

t: Variation in the shape of chloroplast is found in
s: Algae show great variation in chloroplast shape: cup-shaped in Chlamydomonas, spiral ribbon in Spirogyra, girdle-shaped in Ulothrix, stellate in Zygnema, discoid and others. In bryophytes, pteridophytes and gymnosperms chloroplasts are usually uniformly discoid or lens-shaped, so variation in shape is characteristic of algae.

t: Name the storage bodies found in the chloroplast of most of the green Algae
s: Most green algae have one or more storage bodies called pyrenoids in their chloroplasts; they contain protein besides starch. Laminarin is the stored food of brown algae and floridean starch that of red algae. Some algae store food as oil droplets, but these are not the named storage bodies.

t: Presence of polysulphate esters in the cell wall is a character of
s: Red algae (Rhodophyceae) have a cell wall made of cellulose, pectin and polysulphate esters, which provide the gelatinous substances like agar and carrageen. Green algae have cellulose walls, brown algae have cellulose with algin, and blue-green algae are prokaryotes with a different wall.

t: Male gametophyte in Gymnosperm is represented by
s: In gymnosperms the microspores develop into a reduced male gametophyte called the pollen grain within the microsporangium. Microsporangium is the sporophytic structure that produces microspores, nucellus is the tissue of the megasporangium, and endosperm is the female gametophyte tissue.

t:
Which of the following features are related to Gymnosperms?
a) Seeds are naked
b) Main plant body is sporophyte
c) Archegonia and antheridia present
d) Ovules absent
s: Gymnosperms have naked seeds (ovules not enclosed in an ovary) and their main plant body is the sporophyte, so a and b are correct. Ovules are present, so d is wrong. Archegonia are present in the female gametophyte, but antheridia are absent because the male gametophyte is a reduced pollen grain, so c is wrong.

t: Algin, carrageen and starch are obtained from:
s: Algin is obtained from brown algae (e.g. Laminaria, Sargassum), carrageen from red algae (e.g. Chondrus, Gelidium), and starch is the reserve food of green algae (Chlorophyceae). Thus the order is brown algae, red algae and green algae respectively.
o: Red algae, brown algae, green algae respectively
Brown algae, red algae, green algae respectively
Red algae, green algae, brown algae respectively
Green algae, brown algae, red algae respectively

t: In gymnosperms, the strobili bearing microsphorophylls and microsporangia are called
s: In gymnosperms the microsporophylls bearing microsporangia are arranged spirally along an axis to form lax or compact microsporangiate or male strobili (cones). Megasporophylls with ovules form macrosporangiate or female strobili. So strobili with microsporophylls are male strobili.

t: Nature of flagella in Green algae
s: Green algae (Chlorophyceae) bear 2 to 8 flagella that are equal in length and apically inserted. Brown algae have two unequal, laterally attached flagella, and red algae have no flagella. Hence 2 to 8, equal, apical is the correct description.

t:
Statement I - In Pteridophytes, the main plant body is the sporophyte which is differentiated into true root, stem and leaves.
Statement II - In Pteridophytes, the sporophytes bear sporangia that are subtended by leaf-like appendages called sporophylls.
s: Both statements are true. In pteridophytes the main plant body is a diploid sporophyte differentiated into true root, stem and leaves with vascular tissues. The sporophytes bear sporangia that are subtended by leaf-like appendages called sporophylls, which may form compact strobili or cones in some plants.
o: Statement I is true but statement II is wrong
Statement II is true but statement I is wrong

t: After fertilization, ovules develop into ____ A ____ and ovaries develop into ____ B ____ .Identify A and B
s: After double fertilisation in angiosperms, the ovules mature into seeds and the ovary wall and ovary develop into the fruit. The zygote develops into the embryo, and the primary endosperm nucleus develops into the endosperm. Hence A is seeds and B is fruits.

t: Which of the following is not correctly matched?
s: Spirogyra shows non-motile isogamy: the gametes are similar in size but non-flagellated, and they meet through conjugation tubes. Chlamydomonas is unicellular and flagellated, Eudorina shows anisogamy, and Volvox is a colonial motile form, so these pairs are correctly matched.

t: Floridean starch is the stored food in
s: Floridean starch, a carbohydrate very similar in structure to amylopectin and glycogen, is the stored food of red algae (Rhodophyceae). Green algae store starch and oil, while brown algae (Phaeophyceae) store laminarin and mannitol.

t: Which of the following statement is wrong about Bryophytes?
s: The gametophyte is not differentiated into foot, seta and capsule; these are the parts of the moss sporophyte. In bryophytes fertilisation requires water for the swimming antherozoids, the gametophyte is the dominant independent phase, and the sporophyte is attached to and dependent on the gametophyte.
o: Fertilization takes place in presence of water
Gametophytic phase is dominant phase in life cycle
Gametophyte is differentiated into foot, seta and capsule

t: The plant body in brown algae is usually attached to the substratum by :-
s: The plant body of brown algae is usually attached to the substratum by a holdfast, and it has a stalk called the stipe and a leaf-like photosynthetic organ called the frond. Rhizoids occur in bryophytes, while stipe and frond are not attachment organs.

t: A moss which have a great role in providing peat that have long been used as fuel
s: Sphagnum, a moss, provides peat that has long been used as fuel and, due to its water-holding capacity, as packing material for trans-shipment of living material. Marchantia is a liverwort and Funaria a moss without this use, so Sphagnum is correct.

t: Strobili or cones are found in
s: Equisetum has its sporophylls arranged in compact structures called strobili or cones. Pteris and Salvinia bear sporangia on leaves or sporocarps without forming cones, and Marchantia is a liverwort with no cones. So strobili are found in Equisetum, as also in Selaginella.

t:
Select the correctly matched ones :
I. Phaeophyceae - Mannitol
II. Rhodophyceae - Dictyota
III. Chlorophyceae - Non-motile gametes
IV. Rhodophyceae - r - phycoerythrin
s: Brown algae (Phaeophyceae) store food as mannitol and laminarin (I correct). Red algae contain r-phycoerythrin (IV correct). Dictyota is a brown alga, not a red alga (II wrong). Green algae usually form motile flagellated gametes, so non-motile gametes is wrong for Chlorophyceae (III wrong).

t: Algin is found in the cell wall of
s: Algin, a hydrocolloid, is found in the cell walls of brown algae such as Laminaria and is commercially extracted from them. Chara is a green alga, while Gelidium and Polysiphonia are red algae whose walls yield agar, not algin.

t: Which of the following algae are suitable for human consumption?
s: Many species of Porphyra (a red alga), Laminaria and Sargassum (brown algae) are among the 70 or so species of marine algae used as food. Chara, Spirogyra and Fucus are not listed as edible algae, so the pair Porphyra and Sargassum is correct.

t: Archegoniophore is present in
s: Archegoniophore is the stalked female receptacle bearing archegonia in the liverwort Marchantia. Funaria (moss) bears archegonia at the apex of a leafy shoot, Adiantum bears them on a prothallus, and Chara has oogonia, so archegoniophore occurs only in Marchantia.

t: In moss, spore germinate to form
s: In mosses the haploid spore germinates to form the protonema, a creeping, green, branched, filamentous juvenile gametophyte. Lateral buds on the protonema form the leafy gametophyte. Prothallus is the fern gametophyte, and the sporophyte develops from the zygote, not from a spore.

t: Which of the following statement is wrong about Bryophytes?
s: In bryophytes the zygote does not undergo meiosis immediately; it divides by mitosis to form a multicellular diploid sporophyte, and meiosis occurs later in the capsule to form spores. Fertilisation occurs inside the archegonium, the gametophyte is dominant, and the sex organs are multicellular, so these are correct.
o: Gametophytic phase is dominant in life cycle
Zygote undergoes meiosis to produce sporophyte

t: In a moss, the sporophyte
s: In mosses, the sporophyte develops from the zygote on the gametophyte. It is green when young and partly photosynthetic but remains attached to the gametophyte for water and nutrients, so it is partially dependent on it. It produces spores, not gametes, and it does not arise from a spore.
o: arises from a spore produced from the gametophyte
produces gametes that give rise to the gametophyte
is partially depend on the gametophyte
manufactures food for itself, as well as for the gametophyte

t: A moss, which provide peat that have long been used as fuel, and as packing material for trans-shipment of living material
s: Sphagnum, a moss, provides peat that has long been used as fuel, and its high water-holding capacity makes it useful as packing material for trans-shipment of living material. Funaria and Polytrichum are mosses without this use, and Marchantia is a liverwort.

t: Which of the following are heterosporous
s: Selaginella (a lycopod) and Salvinia (a water fern) produce two kinds of spores, small microspores and large megaspores, so they are heterosporous. Psilotum, Pteris and Adiantum are homosporous, producing only one kind of spore. Hence the pair Selaginella and Salvinia is correct.

t: Plants forming spores but lacking seed and vascular tissue are
s: Bryophytes reproduce by spores, but they lack seeds and true vascular tissue (xylem and phloem). Pteridophytes are spore-bearing but have vascular tissue, while gymnosperms and angiosperms produce seeds. So bryophytes are spore-forming plants lacking both seed and vascular tissue.

t: Protonema is the juvenile filamentous stage in the life cycle of
s: Protonema is the creeping, green, branched, filamentous juvenile stage of the gametophyte that develops from the spore in mosses. Funaria and Polytrichum are both mosses, so both show it. Marchantia is a liverwort in which the spore develops directly into a thallus without a typical protonema.

t: Which of the following Pteridophyte is heterophyllous and lack roots?
s: Salvinia is an aquatic water fern that lacks true roots; its submerged leaves are finely dissected and look like roots. It shows heterophylly, with floating entire leaves and submerged root-like leaves. Psilotum lacks roots but is not heterophyllous, while Adiantum and Equisetum have true roots.

t: Which one of the following pairs of plants are not seed producers?
s: Fern (a pteridophyte) and Funaria (a moss) reproduce by spores and do not form seeds. Eucalyptus is an angiosperm and Cycas and Pinus are gymnosperms, all seed producers. Therefore the pair of non-seed producers is fern and Funaria.

t: The independent plant body of bryophyte is
s: In bryophytes the main independent and dominant plant body is the haploid gametophyte, which bears the sex organs. The diploid sporophyte develops from the zygote and remains attached to and dependent on the gametophyte. A sporophyte is never haploid and the gametophyte is never diploid normally.

t: Male gametophyte in Gymnosperm is represented by
s: In gymnosperms the microspores develop into a reduced male gametophyte called the pollen grain within the microsporangium. Microsporangium is the sporophytic structure that produces microspores, nucellus is the tissue of the megasporangium, and endosperm is the female gametophyte tissue.

t: In Pinus, male cone bears a large number of
s: In Pinus the male cone (microsporangiate strobilus) consists of a large number of microsporophylls arranged spirally on a central axis, each bearing microsporangia (pollen sacs). Stamens and anthers belong to angiosperms, and megasporophylls are borne on female cones.

t: Smallest flowering plant is
s: Wolffia, a tiny aquatic angiosperm about 0.1 cm in size, is the smallest flowering plant. Eucalyptus is a very tall angiosperm tree, Sequoia is a tall gymnosperm (not a flowering plant), and Rafflesia has the largest flower.

t:
Identify the following parts correctly
[[img:458aa64ed36d]]
s: The figure shows a female thallus of Marchantia. Part a is the stalked archegoniophore with archegonia, b is the gemma cup bearing gemmae for vegetative reproduction, and c are the rhizoids that anchor the thallus. Liverworts lack true roots, and the umbrella-like structure here is female, not an antheridiophore.
o: a - Anthrediophore, b - Gemma cup , c - Rhizoids
a - Archegoniophore, b - Gemma cup, c - Rhizoids
a - Archegoniophore, b - Gemma cup, c - Root
a - Gemma cup, b - Anthrediophore, c - Rhizoids

t: The endosperm of gymnosperm is:
s: In gymnosperms the endosperm is the female gametophyte tissue formed before fertilisation from the haploid megaspore, so it is haploid. In angiosperms the endosperm forms by fusion of a male gamete with two polar nuclei, making it triploid.

t: Prothallus represents the
s: In ferns the spore germinates to form a small, free-living, mostly photosynthetic thalloid gametophyte called the prothallus, which bears antheridia and archegonia. It is not a sporophyte, and gymnosperms have reduced gametophytes, not a prothallus.

t: Pear shaped zoospores having two unequal laterally attached flagella is a characteristic feature of
s: Brown algae (Phaeophyceae) reproduce asexually mainly by biflagellate zoospores that are pear-shaped and have two unequal, laterally attached flagella. Green algae have 2 to 8 equal apical flagella, red algae have no flagella, and blue-green algae are non-flagellated prokaryotes.

t: Choose the false statement about Pteridophytes
s: In pteridophytes the sporophyte, not the gametophyte, is differentiated into true root, stem and leaves. The gametophyte is a small multicellular, free-living, thalloid prothallus. Pteridophytes grow in cool, damp, shady and also sandy places, and are used as ornamentals, medicinally and as soil binders.
o: They are found in cool, damp, shady places as well as in sandy soil conditions
The gametophyte is differentiated into true root, stem and leaves
They are frequently grown as ornamentals
They are used for medicinal purposes and also as soil binders

t: Find the correct pair from the following
s: Ulothrix is a filamentous green alga, so option D is correct. Chlorella is a unicellular green alga, not a red alga; Volvox is a motile colonial green alga, not a brown alga; and Laminaria is a brown alga, not a red alga.
o: Flattened leaf like Red alga - Laminaria

t: Diploid sporopyte is the dominant phase in
s: In pteridophytes, gymnosperms and angiosperms the diploid sporophyte is the main, dominant, independent plant body, while the gametophyte is reduced, being independent but small in pteridophytes and dependent in seed plants. So all the given groups have a dominant sporophyte.

t: Select the incorrect pair
s: Chemotaxonomy uses the chemical constituents of the plant, such as secondary metabolites, to resolve confusions. Information on chromosome number, structure and behaviour is used in cytotaxonomy. Numerical taxonomy uses all observable characters and phylogenetic taxonomy uses evolutionary relationships, so option C is incorrect.

t:
Read the given statements about algae and select the correct option
i) Plant body is thalloid
ii) Largely aquatic
iii) Reproduction by vegetative, asexual and sexual methods
iv) Some of them associate with fungi and animals
v) Chlamydomonas, Volvox, Ulothrix are the multicellular algae
s: Statements i to iv are true: algae have a thalloid body, are largely aquatic, reproduce by vegetative, asexual and sexual methods, and some associate with fungi (lichens) and animals (sloth bear). Statement v is false because Chlamydomonas is unicellular and Volvox is colonial; only Ulothrix is multicellular filamentous.

t: Which of the following is not correctly matched?
s: Volvox shows oogamy, fusion of a large non-motile egg with a small motile male gamete; it does not show isogamy. Ulothrix shows motile isogamy, Eudorina shows anisogamy, and Spirogyra shows non-motile isogamy, so these pairs are correct.

t: Which of the following groups of algae belongs to class Phaeophyceae?
s: Laminaria, Fucus, Dictyota and Sargassum are all brown algae (Phaeophyceae). Gelidium, Porphyra, Gracilaria and Polysiphonia are red algae, and Volvox, Ulothrix and Spirogyra are green algae, so all the other options include non-phaeophycean members.

t: Kelps are
s: Kelps are large brown algae of class Phaeophyceae, such as Laminaria and Macrocystis, which may reach a height of 100 m. They have a holdfast, stipe and frond and contain fucoxanthin. They are not red, green or blue-green algae.

t: The branch of taxonomy which is carried out using computers, based on all observable characteristics is called
s: Numerical taxonomy is carried out using computers and is based on all observable characteristics. Each character is given a number and code, and many characters are given equal importance. Cladistics uses shared derived characters, cytotaxonomy uses chromosome data and chemotaxonomy uses chemical constituents.

t: Which is a colonial green alga?
s: Volvox is a motile colonial green alga, in which many flagellated cells are arranged in a hollow sphere. Spirogyra and Ulothrix are unbranched filamentous green algae, and Chlamydomonas is a unicellular motile green alga.

t: The adaptation/s of conifers to reduce water loss is/are
s: Conifers reduce water loss through needle-like leaves that give a reduced surface area, a thick cuticle that cuts down transpiration, and sunken stomata. Together these xeric features help them withstand extremes of temperature, humidity and wind, so all the given features are correct.

t:
Match the following columns I, II and III and choose the correct option :
[[img:49d8ba873bcf]]
s: Green algae store starch and have pyrenoids (1-c-ii). Brown algae store mannitol and laminarin and have fucoxanthin (2-b-i). Red algae store floridean starch and have phycoerythrin (3-a-iii). Thus the correct match is 1-c-ii, 2-b-i, 3-a-iii.

t: Which of the following are called vascular cryptogams?
s: Pteridophytes are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues (xylem and phloem), yet they reproduce by spores and do not form seeds or flowers, so they are called vascular cryptogams. Bryophytes and algae lack vascular tissue, and gymnosperms are seed plants (phanerogams).

t: Which of the following statement about bryophytes is correct?
s: In bryophytes the haploid gametophyte is the dominant, independent and photosynthetic phase. The sporophyte is not free-living; it is attached to and dependent on the gametophyte. Bryophytes lack true vascular tissues and do not produce seeds, so the other statements are wrong.

t: The cell wall of green algae consists of
s: In green algae (Chlorophyceae) the rigid cell wall is made of an inner layer of cellulose and an outer layer of pectose. Algin is present in the walls of brown algae, so options containing algin are wrong, and option A reverses the order of layers.

t: Protein core surrounded by layers of starch, found in the chloroplast of green algae are called
s: Pyrenoids are storage bodies located in the chloroplasts of most green algae. They contain a protein core surrounded by starch. Zoospores are asexual spores, while stipe and holdfast are parts of the brown algal thallus, so pyrenoids is the correct answer.

t: Which one correctly matches the plant with its class?
s: Adiantum, a fern, belongs to Pteropsida, as do Dryopteris and Pteris. Psilotum belongs to Psilopsida, Selaginella and Lycopodium to Lycopsida, and Equisetum to Sphenopsida, so the other options are mismatched.

t:
Select the correct statement/s about artificial system of classification :
(a) It separated closely related species
(b) It was given on the basis of habit, colour, number, and shape of leaves
(c) It gave equal weightage to vegetative and sexual characteristics.
s: All three statements are correct. Artificial systems, like that of Linnaeus, were based on a few superficial characters such as habit, colour, number and shape of leaves. They gave equal weightage to vegetative and sexual characters, which is not acceptable because vegetative characters are easily affected by environment, and they often separated closely related species.

t:
Read the following statements with respect to algae:
i) A majority of Green algae form massive plant bodies
ii) Vascular tissues are absent
iii) Most common asexual spore is zoospore
iv) Sexual reproduction can be isogamous, anisogamous, or oogamous.
v) Embryo formation is seen in algae
Which of the above statements are correct?
s: Statements ii, iii and iv are correct: algae lack vascular tissue, the zoospore is the most common asexual spore, and sexual reproduction may be isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous. Statement i is wrong because only a few green algae are massive, and v is wrong because embryo formation is absent in algae.
o: i, ii, iii, iv and v

t: In Mosses, after fertilization, the zygote develops into a sporophyte, consisting of
s: In mosses the zygote develops into a sporophyte differentiated into foot, seta and capsule. The foot anchors it in the gametophyte, the seta is a stalk and the capsule bears spores formed after meiosis. Frond, stipe and holdfast are parts of brown algae, and roots are absent in mosses.

t: Identify the correctly matched pair:
s: Porphyra is a red alga, and red algae owe their colour to the red pigment r-phycoerythrin. Volvox is colonial, not filamentous; Fucus shows oogamy, not isogamy; and Sargassum, a brown alga, has pear-shaped gametes with two lateral flagella, not apical flagella.

t:
Read the following statements and select the correct option.
Statement I: Members of phaeophyceae are found at great depth in oceans.
Statement II: Reserve food material of brown algae is laminarin and mannitol.
s: Statement I is incorrect: brown algae are mostly marine but grow in shallow coastal waters; it is red algae (Rhodophyceae) that can occur at great depths where little light penetrates. Statement II is correct: the reserve food of brown algae is complex carbohydrate in the form of laminarin or mannitol.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

t: In which of the following algae, food is stored in the form of carbohydrate, which is very similar to amylopectin and glycogen in structure ?
s: Porphyra is a red alga, and red algae store food as floridean starch, which is very similar in structure to amylopectin and glycogen. Volvox is a green alga storing starch, while Fucus and Sargassum are brown algae storing laminarin and mannitol.

t:
Assertion (A) : Bryophytes and tracheophytes (vascular plants) have an embryo stage in their life cycle.
Reason (R) : In these plants, zygote undergo mitosis to form embryo.
s: Both are true and R explains A. In bryophytes and in tracheophytes (pteridophytes, gymnosperms and angiosperms) the zygote does not undergo meiosis immediately; it divides by mitosis to form a multicellular embryo that develops into the sporophyte. Algae do not form such an embryo.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are false

t: Accessory pigments present in Brown algae and Red algae are respectively
s: Brown algae contain chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and the brown xanthophyll pigment fucoxanthin. Red algae contain chlorophyll a and d along with the red pigment r-phycoerythrin. Floridean starch and starch are stored foods, not pigments, so fucoxanthin and r-phycoerythrin is correct.

t: In Pinus
s: Pinus is monoecious: male and female cones are borne on the same tree but as separate strobili. Microsporophylls form male cones and megasporophylls form female cones, so they are differentiated and not in the same cone. Cycas, by contrast, is dioecious.
o: Male and female cones are borne on different trees

A) Vascular
B) Haploid
C) Independent
D) Dependent on sporophyte
E) Protonema
s: In homosporous pteridophytes like ferns the spore germinates to form a haploid, free-living, mostly photosynthetic thalloid gametophyte, the prothallus. It is independent of the sporophyte and has no vascular tissue. Protonema is the moss gametophyte, not that of pteridophytes.

It is not terrestrial and has no true roots, and heterosporous forms do not form the typical free-living prothallus of homosporous ferns.

t: Which of the following statement is false?
s: In pteridophytes the sporophyte, not the gametophyte, is differentiated into true root, stem and leaves; the gametophyte is a thalloid prothallus. Most pteridophytes are homosporous, Equisetum has sporophylls aggregated into strobili, and antherozoids need water to reach the archegonia, so these statements are true.

t: A Bryophyte differs from Pteridophyte in
s: Bryophytes lack vascular tissues (xylem and phloem), while pteridophytes are the first vascular plants. Both groups have archegonia, flagellated antherozoids that need water, and free-living gametophytes, so these features do not differentiate them.

t: Gymnosperms differ from Pteridophytes in:
s: Gymnosperms produce seeds (naked seeds) while pteridophytes do not; they reproduce by spores. Both groups are vascular plants with a dominant sporophyte, and pteridophyte gametophytes are independent whereas gymnosperm gametophytes are dependent, so only seed formation is the distinguishing feature listed correctly.

t: Select a hydrocolloid obtained from brown algae
s: Algin is a hydrocolloid (water-holding substance) obtained from brown algae such as Laminaria. Agar and carrageen are hydrocolloids obtained from red algae, agar from Gelidium and Gracilaria and carrageen from Chondrus. Hence only algin comes from brown algae.

t: The flask shaped female sex organs in Bryophytes is called:-
s: The female sex organ in bryophytes is the flask-shaped archegonium, which has a swollen venter containing a single egg and a long neck. The antheridium is the male sex organ, antherozoids are the motile male gametes, and protonema is the juvenile gametophyte of mosses.

t: Which of the following statement is not true with respect to gymnosperms?
s: In gymnosperms the gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence; they remain within sporangia retained on the sporophyte. Only the sporophyte is free-living. Sequoia is one of the tallest trees, pollen is carried by air currents, and the endosperm is a haploid pre-fertilisation tissue.
o: Pollen grains are carried by air currents
Gametophyte and sporophyte both are free-living independent structures

t: How many of the following algae belongs to Rhodophyceae
s: The list of algae is not shown here, but the question tests recognition of Rhodophyceae (red algae) such as Porphyra, Polysiphonia, Gracilaria and Gelidium. Members like Volvox, Ulothrix, Spirogyra and Chara are green, while Laminaria, Fucus, Dictyota and Sargassum are brown. As per the key, three of the listed algae belong to Rhodophyceae.

s: The plant shown is Cycas. It has an unbranched stem, pinnately compound leaves that persist for a few years, and coralloid roots associated with nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria. Cycas is dioecious, not monoecious; it shows sporic, not zygotic, meiosis; and mycorrhizal roots are typical of Pinus.

t: Which of the following statement is incorrect for pteridophytes?
s: Selaginella and Salvinia are heterosporous. Their megaspores and microspores develop into female and male gametophytes that are retained, for variable periods, on the parent sporophyte; they do not form a free-living prothallus. The free-living, photosynthetic prothallus with antheridia and archegonia is found in homosporous pteridophytes.

t: If the dipolid number of a Gymnosperm is 36 . What would be the chromosome number in its endosperm?
s: In gymnosperms the endosperm is the female gametophyte, formed from a haploid megaspore before fertilisation, so it is haploid (n). If 2n = 36, then n = 36/2 = 18. Triploid endosperm with 54 chromosomes occurs only in angiosperms.

t: Which combination is correctly matched?
s: Cycas has specialised coralloid roots associated with nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria (Anabaena, Nostoc). Sphagnum is a moss, not a liverwort; Selaginella is heterosporous, which is the precursor to the seed habit; and Pinus has non-motile male gametes carried by pollen tubes and needle-like leaves.
o: Pinus - Motile sperms - Pinnately compound leaves

t: All seed bearing plants have/show
s: In seed plants (gymnosperms and angiosperms) the gametophytes are highly reduced, few-celled haploid structures that are dependent on the sporophyte, e.g. the pollen grain and the embryo sac. Meiosis occurs in spore mother cells, not zygote, and the dominant phase is the sporophyte, not the gametophyte.
o: Alternation of dominant gametophyte with short lived multicellular sporophyte

t:
Bryophytes show resemblance with algae in
a) Formation of motile sperms
b) Absence of vascular tissues
c) Presence of Haploid gametophyte
s: Bryophytes resemble algae in all three features. Both have motile (flagellated) male gametes that need water, both lack vascular tissues, and in both the main plant body is a haploid gametophyte. Hence a, b and c are all correct.

t: Which of the following is correct sequence of steps involved in life cycle of liverwords if we start from its dominant phase?
s: The step labels are not given in the text, but the life cycle of a liverwort begins with its dominant haploid gametophytic thallus. This bears sex organs that produce gametes, fertilisation forms the zygote, the zygote develops into a sporophyte, the capsule undergoes meiosis to form spores, and the spores germinate to form new gametophytes. The keyed sequence follows this order.

t: Select the common feature amongst Ginkgo, Equisetum and Sphagnum.
s: Ginkgo (gymnosperm), Equisetum (pteridophyte) and Sphagnum (bryophyte) are all archegoniates; the female sex organ is a flask-shaped archegonium. Sphagnum has a dependent sporophyte and lacks vascular tissue, and Ginkgo has a dependent gametophyte, so the other features are not common to all three.

t: Which of the following are heterosporous with dependent male and female gametophyte?
s: Cycas, Pinus and Ginkgo are gymnosperms, which are heterosporous, and their male and female gametophytes are retained in the sporangia and depend on the sporophyte. Adiantum and Dryopteris are homosporous ferns, and Selaginella and Salvinia, though heterosporous, are pteridophytes.

t: Gymnosperms are more advanced than pteridophytes. Which of the following features of gymnosperms, justify this statement?
s: Gymnosperms bear naked seeds, i.e. ovules develop into seeds without an ovary, whereas pteridophytes do not produce seeds at all. Seed habit is a major evolutionary advance. Vascular tissue and a dominant sporophyte are present in both groups, and both have non-motile eggs.

t: Pollen tube is carrier of non-motile male gamete in
s: In gymnosperms such as Pinus, the pollen grain germinates and forms a pollen tube that carries the non-motile male gametes to the archegonia in the ovule. In Sphagnum, Pteris and Fucus the male gametes are motile and swim through water, and no pollen tube is formed.

t: Dioecious (Hetrothallic) liverwort is
s: Marchantia is a dioecious (heterothallic) liverwort with separate male and female thalli bearing antheridiophores and archegoniophores respectively. Funaria is a moss, while Pteris and Selaginella are pteridophytes, not liverworts.

t: Which of the following is not a feature of pteridophytes?
s: Pteridophytes do possess vascular tissues, xylem and phloem; they are the first terrestrial vascular plants. They have an independent sporophyte with true roots, stem and leaves, and water is needed for transfer of antherozoids, so absence of vascular tissue is not their feature.
o: Water is required for transfer of antherozoids

t: In bryophytes
s: In bryophytes the dominant gametophyte is free-living, while the sporophyte remains attached to it and depends on it for water and nutrients. So sporophytes are dependent on gametophytes, not the reverse, and the two generations are not both independent.

t: Which of the following structure/feature is common in Volvox,mosses, ferns and conifers?
s: Volvox, mosses, ferns and conifers all show oogamous sexual reproduction, with a large non-motile egg and a small male gamete. True leaves and vascular bundles are absent in Volvox and mosses, and Volvox, an alga, does not form an embryo.

t: Ginkgo and Cedrus are included in gymnosperms because
s: Ginkgo and Cedrus are gymnosperms because their ovules are not enclosed by an ovary wall and remain exposed before and after fertilisation, so the seeds are naked and not inside a fruit. They have no ovary, so option A is wrong, and their seeds do have seed coats.

Seeds are not protected by seed coats
Seeds do not occur inside the fruit

t: The dominant photosynthetic phase in the life cycle of pteridophyte is the
s: In pteridophytes the main photosynthetic and dominant phase is the diploid sporophyte differentiated into true root, stem and leaves. The gametophyte (prothallus) is haploid, small and short-lived. A gametophyte is never diploid, and a sporophyte is never haploid in a normal life cycle.

t: In Pteridophytes, reduction division occurs when
s: In pteridophytes reduction division (meiosis) occurs in spore mother cells within sporangia, forming haploid spores. The prothallus develops from spores by mitosis, and the haploid gametophyte forms sex organs and gametes by mitosis, so meiosis occurs only at spore formation.

t: Gametophytic plant body is nonvascular in
s: In all plant groups the gametophyte is non-vascular. In algae and bryophytes the whole plant lacks vascular tissue, the fern prothallus has no xylem or phloem, and the reduced gametophytes of gymnosperms and angiosperms (pollen, embryo sac) are non-vascular too. Hence all of these.
